key_insight: The paper reframes 4-bit AdamW optimizer-state quantization in a "rounding space" rather than only analyzing raw state error. This reveals why small average quantization error can still produce meaningful bias in adaptive updates, especially for the second moment near zero.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of compressing AdamW optimizer states to 4 bits without degrading training, by accounting for how quantization errors propagate through the momentum and variance recurrences.
method: Redesign quantization from the perspective of the coordinate space where rounding decisions are made, not just the stored optimizer values.
Analyze the second-moment update locally around the quantization cell adjacent to zero to understand when small state error can still lead to update bias.
Use this analysis to guide more robust 4-bit optimizer-state quantization for AdamW.
impact: This can make training large models more memory-efficient while preserving optimizer behavior. For practitioners, it offers a principled path to lower-memory AdamW without relying on naive quantization assumptions.
visual_elements: Diagram of AdamW moment updates showing where quantization is inserted

paper_title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
paper_authors: Hanyang Li, Shao Tang, Daniel Thomas Braithwaite, Gregory Dexter, Leonardo Neves
